Markets & Conviction

AI Selloff Pulls Bitcoin Below $58,000 as the ‘58k Gang’ Reconvenes

Anthropic’s post-IPO slide drags global tech shares into their worst week since 2020, pulling bitcoin under $58,000 and prompting a tongue-in-cheek reunion across Nostr.

A record-setting Wall Street debut turned into a synchronized global unwind on Friday, dragging bitcoin below $60,000 for the first time since early July and briefly down to $57,655 [s504, s507]. Anthropic, which priced its IPO at $83 and opened at $111.50 on Thursday before closing at $97.17, fell nearly 12 percent to roughly $86 in its first full session, pulling the Nasdaq Composite down about 5 percent and Nvidia down 12.5 percent to near $128 [s504, s507].

Asian markets absorbed the brunt of the tech liquidation: MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan lost roughly 8.3 to 8.5 percent for the week, its steepest drop since March 2020, while Taiwan sank roughly 16 to 17 percent [s504]. Adding to sector jitters, Intuit slashed Credit Karma’s FY2027 growth outlook from 11–13 percent to 3–7 percent after consumers began using large language models instead of its referral site, while agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion [s504, s157]. Capital.com analyst Kyle Rodda said Anthropic's blockbuster IPO proved not enough to assuage the overall concern about the outlook for the AI trade and equities more broadly. [s504]

Bitcoin fell alongside risk assets, trading near $58,300 by Friday afternoon—more than 50 percent off its October 2025 peak above $126,000 and hovering just above its network-wide realized price, the average cost basis of all coins on chain [s507, s509]. Roughly $1.53 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including $1.4 billion in longs, as U.S. spot bitcoin ETF outflows reached $3.5 billion for November following BlackRock IBIT’s record $541.1 million Thursday exit [s507]. Miners with AI data-center exposure fared worst, with MARA Holdings and IREN both falling roughly 17 percent and CleanSpark dropping 16 percent, even as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Federal Reserve not to pursue a half-point rate hike in December [s507, s510].

Across Nostr, the drop drew dry gallows humor rather than panic, reviving the perennial 58k gang chorus across dozens of timelines [s20, s32, s242]. Blast from the past, its like seeing an old friend again after all these years wrote TheBitcoinManual [s252], while Clark Moody declared 58k gang undefeated [s32] and jamw joked about rotating out of ETFs and Strategy into Anthropic shares [s23].

Write down why you own Bitcoin, then ask what the last year actually damaged. If the only answer is the price, nothing you relied on has changed.

That counsel came from Bitcoin Well in a Stoic essay weighing five-year price stagnation against Marcus Aurelius, Epictetus, and Vijay Boyapati’s thesis [s496]. The Stoics drew a firm line between what's in your control and what isn't. The price sits on the far side of it. the company wrote, noting that neither the 21-million supply cap nor permissionless settlement had shifted [s496]. Elsewhere in enforcement news, federal regulators froze assets and charged operators in Kokomo, Indiana, and Gilbert, Arizona, over an alleged $560 million Ponzi scheme that promised 6 percent monthly returns through purported AI-driven currency trading [s511].

Geopolitics

Trump, Xi, and Putin Sign Shenzhen ‘Declaration Toward Peace’

The leaders of the United States, China, and Russia met for roughly 90 minutes at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen on Thursday on the sidelines of APEC, issuing their first formal trilateral statement [s502]. The four-point document calls for United Nations reform, higher production and stable flows of refined petroleum, limits on International Criminal Court jurisdiction paired with state immunity protections, and dialogue to reduce nuclear risks [s502].

The communiqué carries no arms-control framework, implementation timetable, or mention of Ukraine or Iran, and its energy clause makes no reference to dollar-denominated settlement—a framing analysts said could widen non-dollar energy corridors and weaken the enforcement reach of Western sanctions [s502].

Protocol Security

Researchers Publish 131-Page Analysis of Post-Quantum SHRINCS

Blockstream researcher Mikhail Kudinov and co-authors released a 131-page draft security analysis of SHRINCS, a hash-based post-quantum signature proposal combining a stateful FXMSS path (548–4,619 bytes) with a 5,777-byte stateless fallback, compared with 64-byte Schnorr signatures today [s506].

Because reusing a one-time stateful key would allow theft, Blockstream research director Jonas Nick warned wallets must auto-fallback safely and cautioned about block-space pressure: And it’s not just the fee market, it’s also just fewer transactions fit into a block, meaning fewer people can use Bitcoin. And I think this changes the value proposition of Bitcoin. [s506]

Node Operations

Post-Attack Audit Uncovers Over-Broad LNbits Mount and Failing NVMe

After shutting down LNbits during the November 8 incident alert, Core Lightning operator A Rux spent a week auditing their Start9 node with Claude in the terminal and published the findings Saturday morning [s493]. While logs showed no compromise on their own box, the review exposed that LNbits held broad access to node secrets—fixed in Start9 updates and LNbits 1.7.0 via restricted runes—and revealed an internal NVMe drive silently logging SMART failure after writing 568 TB against a 440 TB rating: When something breaks, ask what else could have broken. [s493]

Retail & Settlement

Coffee Shops Lead $13 Median Bitcoin Spend on Square

Block’s report on U.S. Square merchants from November 2025 through October 2026 found a median bitcoin checkout of roughly $13 and an average of $29, with food and drink sellers taking 72 percent of transactions [s505, s508]. Coffee shops and fast-food counters alone drew 62.6 percent of food-and-drink payments at a $9.10 median, while 56.6 percent of all payments—and 66 percent of dollar volume—arrived from external Lightning wallets rather than Cash App [s505, s508].

Block extended zero-fee merchant processing through December 2027 while pressing Congress for a de minimis capital-gains exemption: We think tax policy should account for how people spend bitcoin as well as how they hold it, the company stated [s508].

Elsewhere on Lightning, Amboss detailed how Taproot Assets v0.6 lets edge nodes convert currencies up front while middle hops route ordinary bitcoin: Pay in one asset. Settle in another. One Lightning rail. [s231] On exchange withdrawal checks, nick argued that travel-rule address proofs expose cold-storage multisig signers or xpubs, writing: I think the proper approach to verifying you're paying the correct wallet is to move to signed silent payment addresses. [s15] Brisket countered that regulated exchanges are unlikely to support silent payments for few users when one extra self-transfer restores privacy [s385].

Meanwhile, Fedi advised members of federations upgrading to its new Manifold protocol to move funds between November 30 and December 15 [s14].

Energy & Rights

MIT Study Maps Data-Center Air Mortality to Rural Midwest

A peer-reviewed paper in Environmental Research Letters by MIT, UC Irvine, and Yale researchers estimated that U.S. data-center electricity demand caused roughly 650 modeled premature deaths in 2023—about 5.3 percent of U.S. power-related mortality, within a 559-to-740 confidence interval [s503].

While data centers cluster in northern Virginia and Texas, marginal grid dispatch from Ohio Valley coal and gas plants combines with agricultural ammonia downwind to raise per-capita mortality highest in Iowa, Nevada, South Dakota, and Kansas [s503]. Senior author Noelle Selin warned: Even if you don't think you are affected because there is not a data center near you, think again. [s503]

Surveillance & Rights

Traffic Filters, Section 702, and Breach Fallout

HRF’s AI newsletter reported Russia’s Roskomnadzor spent 2.27 billion rubles (~$28 million) on an AI traffic-filtering system targeting websites and VPNs, alongside Zimbabwe’s expansion of automated traffic enforcement cameras, even as llama.cpp hit v1.0 for local inference [s492]. The Electronic Frontier Foundation urged Congress not to attach Section 702 reauthorization to must-pass defense funding [s173], while Coincards flagged Canada’s Bill C-22 over government access to private messages [s58].

Elsewhere on the privacy front, Signal moved to block screenshots by default so OS-level AI agents cannot read messages [s3], and Base Bitcoin reported a second apparent breach at the FBI’s NCIC criminal database within months [s39].

Ecash Over Sound, Open Miners, and Nostr Compass #49

Developer erik launched Hush Money on magical.cash, encoding 17-byte Cashu ecash redemptions into laptop-played pentatonic tunes in E major that a phone microphone decodes into a Lightning or ecash wallet [s71, s75, s76]. Elsewhere, Canaan previewed MIT-licensed Avalon Nano 3S firmware and a Linux 6.6 SDK for the K230 RISC-V chip [s328], and arkinox published a 10-minute video walkthrough of cyberspace, a thermodynamics-regulated 3D world protocol [s422].
